claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be homogenized at high temperature as a single-phase BCC alloy.
Al and Cr partitioning primarily governs the alloy's phase stability and transformation pathway during cooling and thermal exposure.
Al partitioning promotes formation of the B2 phase.
Cr partitioning promotes formation of the sigma phase.
Sluggish diffusion and local chemical ordering mediate B2 and sigma formation.
Competition between B2 ordering and sigma precipitation determines the phase assemblage after cooling and subsequent thermal exposure.
Al preferentially orders with transition metals to form B2 domains within the BCC matrix.
Atomic diffusion kinetics during cooling and annealing control the extent and morphology of B2 and sigma phases.
Slow cooling or prolonged annealing enhances chemical partitioning and phase separation.
Rapid quenching suppresses chemical partitioning and phase separation.
Rapid quenching from the BCC state should retain a mostly BCC solid solution with minimal B2 or sigma formation.
Relative to rapid quenching, slower cooling will increase the volume fractions of B2 and sigma phases.
Relative to rapid quenching, intermediate-temperature isothermal annealing will increase the volume fractions of B2 and sigma phases.
B2 regions produced during cooling or annealing will be enriched in Al.
Sigma regions produced during cooling or annealing will be enriched in Cr.
The proposed mechanism applies to Cr-rich, Al-containing high-entropy alloys cooled from a single-phase BCC field when B2 and sigma are thermodynamically competitive.
The mechanism should not apply at much lower Al or Cr concentrations, outside the stability ranges of B2 and sigma, or when cooling suppresses essentially all diffusion.
